entries.title: Group O: nO antigens, bOth antibodies
entries.body: Group O red cells are the minimalist of the blood bank: no A, no B — but the plasma has OPINIONS (anti-A and anti-B).
entries.punchline: Like a cat with no manners and all the opinions.
entries.scientificFact: Group O individuals lack A and B transferase activity, leaving unmodified H substance; their plasma contains both anti-A and anti-B isohemagglutinins.

entries.title: GGT: the chaperone of ALP
entries.body: ALP wants to go out (up) but you never know if it's liver or bone — GGT is the chaperone that confirms the liver date.
entries.punchline: Pag walang GGT, bone ang date ni ALP.
entries.scientificFact: GGT is present in hepatobiliary tissue but not in bone; a normal GGT with elevated ALP suggests a bone source.

entries.title: Westgard speed round
entries.punchline: Warning, rejection, rejection — wag makulit sa 2 SD lang!
entries.scientificFact: 1_2s is a warning rule; 1_3s, 2_2s and R_4s are rejection rules in the Westgard multirule framework.

entries.title: The silent haptoglobin
entries.body: When hemolysis happens, haptoglobin disappears without drama. Students look at Hb and miss it every time.
entries.punchline: Low haptoglobin: the quietest scream for help in the lab.
entries.scientificFact: Haptoglobin binds free hemoglobin; in hemolysis it is consumed, becoming undetectable while LDH and indirect bilirubin rise.

entries.title: IgM is too big for the placenta
entries.body: IgM is a pentamer — five units trying to squeeze through the placental gate. Nope.
entries.punchline: IgG: 'Excuse me, passing through.' IgM: 'Bakit ako naiwan?!'
entries.scientificFact: Only IgG crosses the placenta via the FcRn receptor; IgM is restricted to the intravascular space.
